subject: spOccupancy package Data Preparation - single species multi season occupancy

messages.subject: spOccupancy package Data Preparation - single species multi season occupancy
parts:
Hello,

I'm attempting to use the spOccupancy package in R (https://www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/), but I'm having trouble finding the right way to convert my detection/non-detection values as well as the covariates to the format required by the package. I want to use a single-species multi-season spatio-temporal occupancy model (https://www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/reference/stpgocc). 


Data description (attached as sample):
  • I have 96 months of presence/absence data across 4 sites. 'NA' values are used in cases where a survey could not be completed.
  • I have 2 site-level covariates (slope and elevation) for each site
  • I have 2 seasonal covariates (rain and evi) for each site - each season is equivalent to 4 months. In total, 24 observations for each site (96 months / 4)
    • the season duration of 4 months is based on prevalent rainfall conditions and has implications species occurrence

According to the reference document:
  • y is a three-dimensional array with first dimension equal to the number of sites (J), second dimension equal to the maximum number of primary time periods (i.e., years or seasons), and third dimension equal to the maximum number of replicates at a given site.
  • det.covs is a list of variables included in the detection portion of the model, with each list element corresponding to an individual variable. In addition to site-level and/or site/primary time period-level, detection covariates can also be observational-level.
  • Observation-level covariates are specified as a three-dimensional array with first dimension corresponding to sites, second dimension corresponding to primary time period, and third dimension corresponding to replicate

My questions are:
  1. When creating the matrix for y, would the second dimension of primary period be the months (96), seasons (24), or years (96/12) ?
    1. eg: Would the matrix for y, in my case,  be [4, 96,  ], [4, 24,  ], or [4, 8, ].
  2. When creating the matrix for y, would the third dimension for maximum replicates at a site be 24 ( number of seasons), 3 (number of seasons per year), or 4 (number of months per season in a year)?
    1. Would this depend on the value chosen for the second dimension?
    2. How would this influence the formatting of the det.covs as an observation level covariate?

I'm attaching the sample data and code to this message. I hope that someone who has experience with this package could inform me if the conversion looks correct, or if there is anything I could do to improve the analysis methodology.

Code:

PA_96months  <- read.xlsx("./spOccupancy_RepresentativeData.xlsx"
                          , sheetIndex = 2)

PA_24seasons  <- read.xlsx("./spOccupancy_RepresentativeData.xlsx"
                          , sheetIndex = 3)

num_sites <- 4

#creating an empty array
y <- array(NA, dim = c(num_sites , max_primaryperiod, max_replicates))

# if the 96-month presence/absence is used
detection_matrix <- as.matrix( PA_96months[, -1])  # Exclude the "site" column
sites <-  PA_96months$Grid_ID

#if the 24-season presence/absence is used 
detection_matrix <- as.matrix( PA_24seasons[, -1])  # Exclude the "site" column
sites <-  PA_24seasons$Grid_ID

# Loop through the data frame rows and fill the array
for (i in 1:num_sites) {
  site_rows <- which(sites == unique(sites)[i])
 
  if (length(site_rows) > 0) {
    site_data <- as.matrix(detection_matrix[site_rows, ])
   
  # Determine the dimensions for the current site
    num_rows <- nrow(site_data)
    num_cols <- ncol(site_data)
   
    # Fill the array for the current site
    site_data <- y[i, 1:num_rows, 1:num_cols]
  }
}


Thank you

messages.author: 9723aac8fc0c9507
messages.subject: Re: spOccupancy package Data Preparation - single species multi season occupancy
parts:
Hello,

For the case of fitting multi-season models with stPGOcc(), the second dimension is equal to the primary time period over which you allow changes in occupancy, while the third dimension is equal to the number of replicate surveys within a given primary time period in which the occupancy state is assumed to be closed (i.e., the closure assumption). Based on your description of your sample data set, the dimensions of the three-dimensional matrix y should be 4 (sites), season (24), and number of months per season (4). For example, the value y[1, 2, 3] would correspond to the detection (1) or nondetection (0) of the species at site 1 during the third month of season 2. If that site was not sampled during that given season/month, then the value should be NA.  

For the detection covariates, because they only vary by site and season, the individual variables can be formatted as a two-dimensional matrix with rows corresponding to sites (4) and columns corresponding to seasons (24). Looking at the "Covariates" tab of your spreadsheet, you can just pull the columns out related to "rain", and then put this as a matrix into a list for "det.covs":

library(xlsx)
covs <- read.xlsx("./spOccupancy_RepresentativeData.xlsx", sheetIndex = 4)
# Columns that have rain variable
col.indx <- which(substr(colnames(covs), 1, 13) == 'det.covs.rain')
rain.cov <- as.matrix(covs[, col.indx])
# Put into a list for det.covs, can add other variables to the list as necessary
det.covs <- list(rain = rain.cov)

Kind regards,

Jeff
